_comment: GRAFIX run config: produces the actual 'proposed framework' numbers (Table 5) and the component leave-one-out ablation (Table 1a/1b/1c), not the gradient-boosting stand-in. Requires PyTorch: pip install torch. Run: python qedhtn_pipeline.py --config run_grafix.json --outdir grafix_tables --max-cardinality 50
_compute_note: GRAFIX is now MINIBATCHED and inductive: it builds a kNN graph over at most max_train_nodes reference rows, samples knn_k neighbours per example, and trains/infers in batches of batch_size. Cost is O(batch * knn_k), so it scales to PaySim (6.3M) and IEEE-CIS on CPU without building one giant full-graph. Still, start with UCI/ULB to validate, then scale up; a GPU speeds the big two up a lot.
_ablation_note: run_ablation=true runs the leave-one-out over GRAFIX components (-Graph, -GAT, -Transformer, -Fusion) plus the Q-FARM->RBF and Q-FARM->MI feature substitutions, per dataset. This multiplies the number of training runs; expect it to be slow. Set to false first to get just the Table 5 numbers quickly.
_knobs: max_train_nodes caps the reference/graph set (default 200000); batch_size (default 4096), knn_k neighbours (default 10), epochs (default 30). Lower max_train_nodes or batch_size if memory is tight; raise epochs for more training.
